title: The Emergency
subtitle: A Newspaper With a Blank Column
posterMeta: CENSORSHIP AS AN OBJECT THE BLANK SPACE WHERE THE NEWS SHOULD
logline: The Emergency. A democracy suspended in the name of stability; the debate over civil liberty, federalism and memory remains live.

style.look: ink black, newsprint cream, sodium amber, one stamp of red; paper grain, ruling lines, dust in a hard side light
rules: Show the object before the explanation: the page, the register, the lamp, the gate.
No bodies, no blood, no reconstruction of violence. The aftermath carries it.
One idea per shot. The camera pushes, reveals or holds; it never drifts.
Cut on the voice. Do not park on a plate after the narration has stopped.
Every number is an official figure or explicitly attributed to a source.

narration.text: The Delhi edition of the Indian Express carried a blank editorial on 28 June.
narration.quote: The Delhi edition of the Indian Express on 28 June, carried a blank editorial, while the Financial Express reproduced in large type Rabindranath Tagore's poem "Where the mind is without fear".

narration.text: The Financial Express reproduced Rabindranath Tagore's poem Where the mind is without fear in large type.
narration.quote: The Delhi edition of the Indian Express on 28 June, carried a blank editorial, while the Financial Express reproduced in large type Rabindranath Tagore's poem "Where the mind is without fear".

narration.text: More than 100,000 political opponents, journalists and dissenters were imprisoned.
narration.quote: More than 100,000 political opponents, journalists and dissenters were imprisoned.

narration.text: The central government imposed strict censorship on radio, television and newspapers during this period.
narration.quote: The central government also imposed censorship on radio, television and newspapers.

narration.text: All publications were subjected to substantial censorship by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
narration.quote: Police were granted powers to impose curfews and detain citizens indefinitely, and all publications were subjected to substantial censorship by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

scenes.title: The order
scenes.purpose: Show the decision, who made it, and the words it was made in.

narration.text: Ahmed declared a State of Emergency caused by internal disorder based on Article 352(1) of the Constitution on 25 June 1975.
narration.quote: Accordingly, Ahmed declared a State of Emergency caused by internal disorder, based on the provisions of Article 352(1) of the Constitution, on 25 June 1975.

narration.text: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed officially issued the Emergency under Article 352 of the Constitution because of a prevailing Internal Disturbance.
narration.quote: Officially issued by president Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed under Article 352 of the Constitution of India because of a prevailing "Internal Disturbance", the Emergency were in effect from 25 June 1975 and ended on 21 March 1977.

narration.text: Indira Gandhi requested President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to proclaim a state of emergency later that day.
narration.quote: Later that day, Indira Gandhi requested a compliant President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to proclaim a state of emergency.

narration.text: She got the President to issue Ordinances completely bypassing the Parliament, allowing her to rule by decree when laws seemed too slow.
narration.quote: And when she felt the existing laws were 'too slow', she got the President to issue 'Ordinances' - a law-making power in times of urgency, invoked sparingly - completely bypassing the Parliament, allowing her to rule by decree.

narration.text: Siddhartha Shankar Ray proposed to the prime minister to impose an internal emergency as Chief Minister of West Bengal.
narration.quote: Siddhartha Shankar Ray, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, proposed to the prime minister to impose an "internal emergency".

scenes.title: The machine
scenes.purpose: Explain how the decision reached ordinary life: the law, the police, the press.

narration.text: The government introduced press censorship, postponed elections and banned strikes and rallies.
narration.quote: However, the government introduced press censorship, postponed elections and banned strikes and rallies.

narration.text: Within three hours, the electricity to every major newspaper was cut.
narration.quote: Within three hours, the electricity to all major newspapers was cut and the political opposition was arrested.

narration.text: Police forces were empowered to make warrantless searches and arrests.
narration.quote: Curfews were imposed and police forces were empowered to make warrantless searches, seizures and arrests.

narration.text: Under MISA, 34,988 people were arrested; under DISIR, 75,818.
narration.quote: During the emergency, 34,988 people were arrested under MISA, and 75,818 people were arrested under DISIR.

narration.text: The Government placed thousands of protestors and strike leaders under preventive detention.
narration.quote: The Government used police forces across the country to place thousands of protestors and strike leaders under preventive detention.

scenes.title: The cost
scenes.purpose: Count what it took, in the terms the record uses, without inventing a figure.

narration.text: Amnesty International recorded 140,000 arrests without trial during the twenty months of the Emergency.
narration.quote: According to Amnesty International, 140,000 people had been arrested without trial during the twenty months of Gandhi's Emergency.

narration.text: Teenagers faced imprisonment, with one sixteen-year-old detained for over eleven months.
narration.quote: Many cases where teens were arrested and imprisoned have come to light, one such example is of Dilip Sharma who, at age 16, was arrested and imprisoned for over 11 months.

narration.text: The sterilization program reached 8.3 million procedures in 1976 and 1977, mostly forced.
narration.quote: In 1976-1977, the program led to 8.3 million sterilisations, most of them forced, up from 2.7 million the previous year.

narration.text: Rajan from the Regional Engineering College suffered torture and died while in police custody.
narration.quote: Rajan of the Regional Engineering College, Calicut, was arrested by the police in Kerala on 1 March 1976, tortured in custody until he died and then his body was disposed of and was never recovered.

narration.text: The commission found that vagabonds and beggars were forced into sterilization clinics by Youth Congress workers and the police.
narration.quote: The commission found that vagabonds and beggars were forced into sterilization clinics during the emergency by Youth Congress workers and the police.

scenes.title: The turn
scenes.purpose: Find the moment the order broke: the election, the release, the first page printed again.

narration.text: Mrs Indira Gandhi called elections for March and released all political prisoners on 23 January 1977.
narration.quote: On 23 January 1977, Mrs Indira Gandhi called elections for March and released all political prisoners.

narration.text: The Janata party won a sweeping victory on 23 March, securing 43.2% of the popular vote.
narration.quote: On 23 March, it was announced that the Janata party had won a sweeping victory, securing 43.2% of the popular vote and 271 seats.

narration.text: The Janata Party manifesto promised to restore the Constitution to its pre-Emergency condition in the 1977 elections.
narration.quote: In its election manifesto for the 1977 elections, the Janata Party promised to "restore the Constitution to the condition it was in before the Emergency and to put rigorous restrictions on the executive's emergency and analogous powers".

narration.text: Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress prime minister after the party defeated the Congress (R) in 1977.
narration.quote: In the 1977 general election, the party defeated the Congress (R) and JP leader Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress prime minister in independent modern India's history.

narration.text: The Janata alliance claimed the elections were India's last chance to choose between democracy and dictatorship.
narration.quote: The Janata alliance, with Jai Prakash Narayan as its spiritual guide, claimed the elections were the last chance for India to choose between "democracy and dictatorship".

scenes.title: The argument
scenes.purpose: Put the dispute on the table: who defended it, who fought it, and on what ground.

narration.text: Indira Gandhi defended the emergency as essential for national security despite offering apologies for abuses.
narration.quote: Although she offered apologies for abuses committed during the Emergency, Indira and the Congress (R) defended the rationale of imposing the state of emergency as being essential for national security.

narration.text: Critics condemned her authoritarian rule and cult of personality during the Emergency period.
narration.quote: Critics note her cult of personality and authoritarian rule of India during the Emergency.

narration.text: The 42nd Amendment faced widespread criticism for clamping down on civil liberties and human rights.
narration.quote: The 42nd Amendment was widely criticised, and the clampdown on civil liberties and widespread abuse of human rights by police angered the public.

narration.text: The amendment deprived citizens of direct access to the Supreme Court except for fundamental rights violations.
narration.quote: The most controversial issue was the 42nd amendment to the Constitution of India, which deprived citizens of direct access to the Supreme Court, except when violation of the fundamental rights resulted from Union law.

narration.text: In a seven-to-six decision, the Supreme Court restricted Parliament's power to alter the Constitution's basic structure.
narration.quote: With a wafer-thin majority of 7 to 6, the bench of the Supreme Court restricted Parliament's amendment power by stating it could not be used to alter the "basic structure" of the Constitution.

scenes.title: The record
scenes.purpose: Show what was written down, and what the writing left out.

narration.text: The Shah Commission began hearing oral evidence from witnesses starting on 29 September 1977.
narration.quote: Starting on 29 September 1977 the commission began hearing oral evidence of witnesses.

narration.text: It found that the Maintenance of Internal Security Act and Defence of India Rules were abused against political opponents.
narration.quote: The commission concluded that during the Emergency the provisions of the Maintenance of Internal Security Act and the Defence of India Rules were not followed but were abused in order to damage political opponents.

narration.text: The final report issued on 6 August 1978 covered prison conditions, torture, and family planning atrocities.
narration.quote: The final report was issued on 6 August 1978 and covered prison conditions, torture and family planning atrocities.

narration.text: Critics later argued that the commission confused investigation with inquiry.
narration.quote: The Shah commission was later criticized for confusing investigation with inquiry.

narration.text: The commission missed its initial 31 December 1977 deadline and received an extension to 30 June 1978.
narration.quote: The commission was to report by 31 December 1977, but was later given an extension to 30 June 1978.

scenes.purpose: Return to the opening object: what survived, what was withdrawn, what is still on the record.

narration.text: Indira Gandhi returned to power in January 1980 after a landslide election victory.
narration.quote: After Indira Gandhi returned to power in a landslide election victory in January 1980, the Supreme Court found that the special courts were not legally constituted, so no trials were conducted.

narration.text: Parliament passed an act on 8 May 1979 establishing two special courts.
narration.quote: Parliament eventually passed an act establishing two special courts on 8 May 1979.

narration.text: The Supreme Court ruled the special courts were not legally constituted, halting all proceedings.
narration.quote: After Indira Gandhi returned to power in a landslide election victory in January 1980, the Supreme Court found that the special courts were not legally constituted, so no trials were conducted.

narration.text: Indira Gandhi attempted to recall copies of the Shah Commission report wherever possible.
narration.quote: As per Hewitt, Indira Gandhi attempted to recall copies of the report wherever possible.

narration.text: The Indian Express carried a blank editorial on 28 June during the Emergency.
